Verdict: ACCEPTThe displayed dual-guard theorem, including the external-charge term  $\tau$ , is correct. Both guard patterns produce actual surviving unit-deficit tiles when unmarked, the donor-tile and degree-four-tail counts are injective, and the quantitative improvement over the previous finer bound is exactly the number of unmarked right sides.The concrete family consequences and the  $32\times32$  cross-component payment example also check from their coordinate constructors.Two small prose qualifications should be made: “strict slack” requires the displayed lower bound to be positive, and §5’s “Each side remains one actual physical unit” should say “Each unmarked side contributes one actual physical unit.” Neither changes equations (4)–(6) or their proof. I give the precise replacements below.1. The hypotheses support the external-charge ledgerLet the original module indices be partitioned into covered modules and additional modules. The definitions give
$$\sum_{\text{covered }i}\rho_i=N-S,
\qquad
\sum_{\text{additional }i}\rho_i=\tau.$$
Every original occupied site remains occupied: an original selection either remains selected or becomes an endpoint, and original endpoints remain endpoints. Thus
$$A_i\subseteq A$$
for every original module, including an additional one. Every final endpoint consequently has occupied degree three or four.A degree-four endpoint has exactly one newly occupied neighbor. That neighbor must be a foreign endpoint. A retained foreign selection would already touch its own persistent endpoint anchor, so touching this endpoint as well would violate final selected feasibility. Optional added selections are expressly prohibited from having endpoint neighbors.The physical incidence ledger therefore applies to the complete original module family. Writing  $E_{\mathrm{in}}$  for the number of intratile foreign endpoint edges, its constituent identities are
$$|R|=\sum_i|R_i|-E_{\mathrm{in}}+J$$
and
$$t_R=\sum_i t_i-2E_{\mathrm{in}}+K.$$
The second identity counts original module–selection incidences. A consumed site shared by several original selected sets contributes once for each such incidence. Missing incidences at intratile foreign-edge orientations are counted by their degree-four tail endpoints, giving exactly  $K$ .Matching sizes add, so
$$\boxed{\rho_{\mathrm{final}}=N-S+\tau-2J+K.}$$
There is no further component correction. The expression already sums the complete physical receiver charges, whether original modules remain separate or merge into common final endpoint components.Optional added selections cause no omitted receiver term: the final receiver union equals the union of the original receiver tiles because the endpoint set is exactly the union of the original endpoint sets. Such additions are outside this union and are accounted for through  $D$ .Finally,  $\tau$  is a signed total original charge. No assumption  $\tau\ge0$  is needed. Negative additional charge helps the same inequality.2. Both protected patterns are valid at every stated width and height2.1 Positive phase and unequal heightsFor the two-leg constructor with leg heights  $a,b$ , put
$$n=\frac{a+b}{2}.$$
Its matching size is  $w+n-1$ . Direct physical tile counting gives:Translation phaseReceiver tilesReceiver selectionsCharge $(0,0)$  $w/2+n+1$  $n+4$  $1$  $(0,1)$  $w/2+n$  $n$  $-1$  $(1,0)$  $w+n$  $n+2$  $1-w$  $(1,1)$  $w+n-2$  $n-2$  $1-w$ Thus the positive case is exactly the reference phase, up to the tile-preserving transports in the construction. The formula depends on the sum of the leg heights and does not require them to be equal.The supplied rotor has charges  $-2,0,0,0$  in its four phases. Consequently the definition
$$S=N-\sum_{\text{covered }i}\rho_i\ge0$$
is justified for all the covered modules. These counts follow from the source constructors in the earlier attachment, independently of any verdict or computational receipt.    physical-fusion-opposed-bands2.2 The two donor tiles are genuinely differentIn reference coordinates, the donor tiles are
$$Q_L=\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\},
\qquad
Q_R=\{2,3\}\times\{w-2,w-1\}.$$
Their selected sites are
$$x_L=(3,2),\qquad x_R=(3,w-1).$$
Because  $w\ge6$ , these are different physical tiles. At the minimum width,
$$Q_L=\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\},
\qquad
Q_R=\{2,3\}\times\{4,5\}.$$
They are adjacent but disjoint.The reflection
$$C(r,c)=(r,w+1-c)$$
preserves the physical tiling because  $w+1$  is odd. It exchanges the two patterns, with the corresponding exchange of leg heights. Unequal heights do not affect either local pattern: both legs contain rows two, three, and four.2.3 Every protecting endpoint has the asserted unique blank neighborOn the left,  $(2,1)$  has original occupied neighbors
$$(1,1),\quad(3,1),\quad(2,0),$$
so its unique blank neighbor is  $(2,2)$ .At minimum left height four,  $(4,1)$  has original occupied neighbors
$$(3,1),\quad(4,0),\quad(5,1).$$
The last two are supports. At greater height, the lower neighbor is an endpoint instead. In either case, the unique blank neighbor remains  $(4,2)$ .The guard  $q_L=(1,3)$  has three original endpoint neighbors
$$(0,3),\quad(1,2),\quad(1,4),$$
and unique blank neighbor  $(2,3)$ .Reflection proves the corresponding right statements. In particular, at  $w=6$ , the two saturated guards are the distinct adjacent endpoints
$$(1,3),\qquad(1,4).$$
Their adjacency does not identify them or their loss events.The six relevant protector/blank pairs are therefore:ProtectorUnique original blank neighbor $(2,1)$  $(2,2)$  $(4,1)$  $(4,2)$  $(1,3)$  $(2,3)$  $(2,w)$  $(2,w-1)$  $(4,w)$  $(4,w-1)$  $(1,w-2)$  $(2,w-2)$ Every pair crosses a physical tile boundary:On the left stem, columns  $1,2$  belong to different tiles.On the right stem, even  $w$  puts columns  $w-1,w$  in different tiles.For both guards, rows  $1,2$  belong to different tiles.All six protectors are different. The row-two and row-four pairs have different columns, and the row-one guards have columns  $3$  and  $w-2\ge4$ .3. An unmarked side gives an actual surviving unit donorConsider the left side; the right proof is its reflected version.If the side is unmarked, its two stem protectors remain degree three. Since all their original occupied neighbors persist, their original blank neighbors
$$(2,2),\qquad(4,2)$$
remain blank.If  $x_L=(3,2)$  became an endpoint, its only possible occupied neighbors would then be
$$p_L=(3,1),\qquad(3,3).$$
It would have occupied degree at most two, contradicting the minimum final endpoint degree of three.Thus  $x_L$  remains selected.Final feasibility now keeps its adjacent tile corners blank. The guard  $q_L=(1,3)$ , also unmarked, remains degree three and preserves its unique original blank neighbor
$$z_L=(2,3).$$
Consequently  $Q_L$  contains exactly one selected site and no endpoints.This argument is robust to additional modules and optional added selections. Any attempted occupation of a prohibited corner would either mark a protector or violate final feasibility. It also does not require degree preservation at the anchor  $p_L$  itself.The same proof holds on the right. Therefore every unmarked side contributes an actual endpoint-free tile of deficit one.Distinctness across modulesWithin a module, the left and right donor tiles are distinct by the coordinate calculation above.Suppose donor tiles from two different modules coincided. Since each is proved to contain exactly one selected site, their selected sites would coincide. That retained selection would touch both original endpoint anchors. Those anchors persist and are distinct because original endpoint sets are disjoint. This contradicts selected feasibility.Hence the tile map from unmarked sides to physical donor tiles is injective.There is one background fact worth stating explicitly when passing to  $D$ : every other endpoint-free tile has nonnegative deficit. Three selected corners in a  $2\times2$  tile would give one selection two occupied neighbors, so such a tile contains at most two selections.Thus the  $2N-G$  distinct unit contributions cannot be offset by negative deficits elsewhere:
$$\boxed{D\ge2N-G.}$$
No donor allocation convention or receiver ownership assumption enters this proof.4. The degree-four loss endpoints are not reusedIndex marked sides by pairs  $(i,s)$ , where  $s\in\{L,R\}$ . For each marked side choose one degree-four protector
$$p_{i,s}\in A_{i,s}.$$
The resulting endpoint map is injective:Within a positive module, the two protector sets are disjoint.Across original modules, the endpoint sets are disjoint.Each chosen endpoint has exactly one new occupied neighbor. It must be its listed original blank neighbor, and that neighbor is outside its physical tile. Hence every chosen endpoint is an intertile degree-four tail.Let
$$V_{4,\mathrm{in}}
=\{p:\deg_A(p)=4,\ \text{the new neighbor of }p\text{ lies in }p\text{’s tile}\}.$$
Then  $|V_{4,\mathrm{in}}|=K$ , and the  $G$  chosen protecting tails lie in its complement within the degree-four endpoint set.Therefore
$$\boxed{K+G\le d_4.}$$
This proves exactly the needed nonduplication statement. Several events may have a common new-neighbor head site; that is harmless because the injection counts their distinct tail endpoints.Likewise, several protectors of one side may become degree four, but that side contributes only one chosen tail and only one unit to  $G$ .5. The external-charge theorem and improvement follow exactlySubstituting the actual donor lower bound into the physical ledger gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma
&=D-\rho_{\mathrm{final}}\\
&\ge(2N-G)-(N-S+\tau-2J+K)\\
&=\boxed{N+S+2J-K-G-\tau}\\
&\ge\boxed{N+S+2J-d_4-\tau}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus
$$\boxed{K+G+\tau\le N+S+2J}$$
is sufficient for the coefficient-one half-area bound. So is the coarser condition
$$d_4+\tau\le N+S+2J.$$
The accounting separates the physical contributions correctly:The actual endpoint-free donor units are the  $2N-G$  unmarked-side tiles. $S$  and  $\tau$  enter through original module charges. $J$  enters once through the receiver correction  $-2J$ . $K$  enters once through missing intratile support incidences.In particular, no full endpoint tile is converted into an extra donor.Exact comparison with the previous finer creditFor  $\tau=0$ , the old left-side count is  $L=G_L$ . Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
B_{\mathrm{new}}-B_{\mathrm{old}}
&=\bigl[N+S+2J-K-G_L-G_R\bigr]\\
&\quad-\bigl[S+2J-K-G_L\bigr]\\
&=\boxed{N-G_R}.
\end{aligned}$$
This is precisely the number of unmarked right sides and lies between zero and  $N$ .The improvement is in the certified lower bound for the same physical slack. It does not change the configuration’s actual  $\sigma$ , and it does not by itself prove the existence of a new configuration satisfying the new sufficient criterion while failing the old one.For the corresponding coarse scalar bound, the gain over  $S+2J-d_4$  is exactly  $N$ .6. The family consequences have the stated valuesThe consequences can also be checked directly as “guaranteed donor capacity minus exact receiver charge”:FamilyExact  $\rho_{\mathrm{final}}$ Guaranteed unmarked donor unitsNew guaranteed slackPrevious creditFour-way cycle $2$  $8$  $6$  $2$ Rotor star $2$  $8$  $6$  $2$ Chain of  $k$  stars $k+1$  $8k$  $7k-1$  $3k-1$ Occupied adjacent bands $2-w$  $2$  $w$  $w-1$ Canonical opposed bands $2-w$  $0$  $w-2$  $w-2$ Here are the source-level checks behind the less immediate entries.Rotor starThe four arms are tile-preserving quarter-turn images of the initial translated positive two-leg module. Each has charge  $1$ ; the central rotor has charge  $-2$ .The only foreign endpoint edges join arm ports to rotor leaves. They are four separate bridges, with mutual support replacement and no new mixed full tile. The coordinate separation remains valid at  $w=6$ : near adjacent arms, potentially neighboring extreme supports occur on different row parities or outside one another’s boundary ranges.Hence
$$N=4,\quad S=2,\quad J=K=G=0,$$
giving credit six.ChainFor the supplied chain constructor, the connector is the transposed width-fourteen two-leg module translated by  $(-25,0)$ . Its effective source phase is  $(0,1)$ , so its charge is  $-1$ .Its ports
$$(-24,4),\qquad(-11,4)$$
join exactly the neighboring star ports
$$(-24,5),\qquad(-11,5).$$
The other occupied sites are separated. Subsequent row shifts by  $-40i$  and alternating reflections  $c\mapsto5-c$  preserve the physical tiling and the same local contacts.Thus the complete original module list has  $4k$  positive arms,  $k$  charge- $-2$  rotors, and  $k-1$  charge- $-1$  connectors:
$$\sum_i\rho_i=4k-2k-(k-1)=k+1.$$
Therefore
$$N=4k,\qquad S=3k-1.$$
All endpoints retain degree three and the contacts form a tree, so  $J=K=G=0$ , giving  $7k-1$ . These are symbolic properties of the supplied all- $k$  constructor.    physical-fusion-opposed-bandsOccupied adjacent bandsTheir degree-four tails occur at odd rows one and three in columns zero and one. None is among the positive module’s six protectors, including at  $w=6$ .Consequently
$$G=0,\quad N=1,\quad S=w-1,\quad J=2,\quad K=4,$$
and
$$N+S+2J-K-G=w.$$
The  $2J=4$  correction cancels  $K=4$  once. The extra unit comes from the surviving right donor.Canonical opposed bandsThe positive module is the larger  $B$ -module of source width  $W=w+2$ , transported by
$$(r,c)\mapsto(h+3-r,c).$$
Its two donor selections map to
$$(h,2),\qquad(h,w+1).$$
Both are actual endpoints of translated  $A$ , so both are consumed.On each side, both stem protectors become degree four while the saturated guard remains degree three. Thus
$$G_L=G_R=1,\qquad G=2.$$
The new credit is
$$1+(w-1)-2=w-2,$$
and its difference from the old credit is  $N-G_R=0$ .This correctly preserves the opposed-band obstruction: the second guard does not provide a surviving donor in that family.7. $$[0,5]\times[0,7].$$
The translated second module occupies sites within
$$[0,5]\times[12,19].$$
The raw width-six rotor star occupies sites within  $[-4,9]^2$ . Translation by  $(16,16)$  places it within
$$[12,25]^2.$$
Thus all three components fit inside coordinates  $0,\ldots,31$ , and their occupied sets are separated by more than one grid step. There are no new contacts between them.The star is eligible to be treated as one additional original module: its endpoint graph is connected, its endpoints have occupied degree exactly three, and every retained selection has exactly one endpoint neighbor.Its internal arm/rotor decomposition may be used to calculate its charge, but those internal modules are not also counted among the covered modules in this application. This is why the example has  $N=2$ , not six.7.2 Freezing does not need to be inherited from a verdictThe two-leg matching is forced by peeling the even stems from their leaves, followed by the alternating bar forcing. The rotor matching is forced by its four leaves.In the star, each intermodule bridge separates even-order unions of original modules. A perfect matching cannot use such a bridge, since that would leave an odd number of vertices on each side. The star therefore has a unique perfect matching.For completeness, uniqueness gives the required freezing here by a direct mixed-promotion argument. Any promoted endpoint would have to lose at least two of its original three occupied neighbors. At least one lost neighbor is not its own mate. That lost endpoint must be the mate of another promoted endpoint. Following these relations produces a directed cycle, and hence an alternating cycle for the original matching, contradicting uniqueness. This argument permits simultaneous promotions and both endpoint colors.The three separated components therefore retain the asserted freezing.7.3 The four assigned donor tiles are explicit and distinctThe payment uses:DonorPhysical tileSole selected siteAssigned chargeFirst module, left $\{2,3\}\times\{2,3\}$  $(3,2)$ First module’s unitFirst module, right $\{2,3\}\times\{4,5\}$  $(3,5)$ First star unitSecond module, left $\{2,3\}\times\{14,15\}$  $(3,14)$ Second module’s unitSecond module, right $\{2,3\}\times\{16,17\}$  $(3,17)$ Second star unitEach tile has exactly one selection and no endpoint. Thus

\rho_{\mathrm{final}}=4.$$
There are  $256-49=207$  endpoint-free tiles and  $60-44=16$  selections outside receivers. Therefore
$$D=2\cdot207-16=398,$$
while
$$\sigma=512-60-58=394=D-\rho_{\mathrm{final}}.$$
With the declared classification,
$$N=2,\quad S=J=K=G=0,\quad\tau=2,$$
the theorem certifies  $\sigma\ge0$ . The four named unit donors indeed pay total charge four. They are not asserted to exhaust the much larger actual deficit.The assignment establishes precisely the claimed global payment. It requires no adjacency between a donor and the receiver whose scalar charge it pays, and establishes no receiver-labelled Hall or flow property.8. Precise prose qualificationsThe formal inequalities are correct as written. For complete precision, I recommend these two replacements.First, qualify strict positivity.Replace the sentence about  $\tau=K=G=0$  with:If  $\tau=K=G=0$ , then  $\sigma\ge N+S+2J$ . This certifies strict positivity whenever  $N+S+2J>0$ , in particular whenever at least one positive covered module is present.The full hypotheses allow a zero-bound case. For example, with an empty module family in a  $2\times2$  rectangle, take the two checkerboard sites as optional added selections. Then all displayed counts are zero and
$$\sigma=2-2=0.$$
This does not contradict the theorem’s weak inequalities; it only shows why an unconditional assertion of strict positivity would be too strong.Second, restrict the physical-unit wording to unmarked sides.Replace §5’s “Each side remains one actual physical unit” with:Each unmarked side contributes one distinct actual endpoint-free unit-deficit tile. An assignment may use each such tile at most once.Marked sides supply no guaranteed unit, as the opposed-band example itself demonstrates.With these wording qualifications, the new argument has the stated scope: it proves a stronger physical compensation budget with exact nonduplication, including signed additional charge, while leaving general decomposition, universal sufficient criteria, and constrained donor ownership unasserted.
